problem: 'Shared-memory SIMD algorithms' mixes two separate ideas. SIMD is about one instruction stream over many data items, not about shared memory, so a student may think SIMD requires shared memory or is a memory model.
fix: SIMD algorithms apply the same operation to many array elements at once. A vector sum, an image filter, or a matrix row update is written as lane-wise work.

problem: The lead and the table say there are four Flynn classes, but the tree shows only SISD, SIMD and MIMD as children; MISD appears only as a small note on the root. A student revising from the figure alone can miss MISD.
fix: Add MISD as a fourth child of the root (note 'many instr, 1 data', edge 'rare, theoretical') so the tree matches the four classes, and keep Dataflow marked as not Flynn.

problem: Chapter 1.3 and Chapter 1.8 are named in plain text instead of being links, so the reader cannot jump to them from the phone.
fix: Write them as Chapter 1.3 and Chapter 1.8.
